In summary, while the water quality at Wollaston Beach in Quincy has been generally good over the past two years, there have been some instances of poor water quality, particularly in 2022. It is essential to monitor the beach's water quality regularly to ensure public safety and maintain the quality of the beach environment.```

According to their guidelines, the Enterococci level should not exceed 104 colonies per 100 milliliters (104 CFU/100mL) on more than 10% of the samples collected during the bathing season.

However, it's important to note that the data provided in the context shows Enterococci levels exceeding this standard at Wollaston Beach on multiple occasions. Specifically, the levels were above 104 CFU/100mL on 2003-08-12, 2003-08-02, 2003-08-08, and 2003-08-18 at Wollaston @ Sachem Street (DCR), and on 2003-07-12 at Wollaston @ Channing Street (DCR).

As for other beaches with similar data, the data provided shows high Enterococci levels at Wollaston @ Milton Street (DCR) in 2006. Specifically, the levels were above 104 CFU/100mL on 2006-08-27.

For more comprehensive and up-to-date information, I would recommend visiting the MassDEP's Beach Program website at https://www.mass.gov/service-details/beach-program. There, you can find current water quality data for various beaches in Massachusetts, as well as information on swimming standards and advisories.```
